blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY — The City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) has placed its firefighting equipment on standby as it anticipates a possible increase in grass fires amid the extreme heat associated with super El Niño, according to the Provincial Information Office Mimaropa- Palawan on Friday, Oct. 2. CDRRMO chief Earl Timbancaya said the city currently records an average of three grass-fire incidents daily, but the number could increase as temperatures rise and vegetation dries out. Timbancaya warned that dried leaves and grass that had been cleared and burned could pose a fire hazard during periods of excessive heat. Even […]...
